grade.primary_choice: Separate TypeScript worker on a BullMQ/Redis queue, Fly process group, stored PDFs, pre-rendered at month close
unsupported_claims: 'Spread over a few hours, that's roughly one core': 20 CPU-minutes over about 3 hours averages close to 0.1 core, so this overstates the load by about 10x (bursts aside)
'A Go rewrite might cut 400 ms to 100 ms' is a guessed speed-up with no measurement behind it, though it is hedged and used to argue against the rewrite

'Per-invocation pricing makes [serverless] awkward at this scale' is doubtful, since about 3,000 invocations a month would cost very little; cold starts and Chromium bundle size are the real objections
grade.notes: Strong answer: it names the event-loop root cause, does the maths, reuses Redis/BullMQ on a Fly process group, stores and pre-renders PDFs, keeps TypeScript with a measurement-gated path to revisit, and lists clear unknowns. Small gaps: it never mentions job timeouts, queue-depth monitoring, or worker autoscaling/scale-to-zero, and its 'roughly one core' figure is too high.
